run.question: In Loki, run the query `{service="checkout"}` against namespace app-282 and tell me how many error-level log lines come back. If the selector returns nothing, find the right one.

report.summary: The selector exactly as given, {service="checkout"}, returned no data for namespace app-282; the streams in that namespace do not use a 'service' label. A namespace-wide query over the same window shows the actual label set: acme_service="checkout", job="checkout-logs", filename="/var/log/checkout.log", level, namespace and pod=checkout-698c8f5df-bg46s. With the corrected selector {acme_service="checkout", namespace="app-282", level="ERROR"}, 4 error-level log lines come back (confirmed by both a line query, which returned 4 lines, and a sum(count_over_time(...[1h])) metric query, which returned 4). Over the same one-hour window the checkout stream contains 16 lines in total: 10 INFO, 2 WARN and 4 ERROR, all from pod checkout-698c8f5df-bg46s. All four ERROR lines fall within the same second, 2026-11-23T19:08:33Z, and their messages name four different failure topics (payment token refused, inventory check timeout, orders-table deadlock on persistence, webhook retries exhausted for partner ACME). Those messages are only checkout's own log text; no dependency (payment, inventory, database, webhook partner) was queried, so nothing is concluded about their state. The count covers only the one-hour window 2026-11-23T18:09:06Z to 19:09:06Z, not the full authorized window.

claims.text: In namespace app-282 the Loki streams for checkout carry the labels acme_service="checkout", job="checkout-logs", filename="/var/log/checkout.log", level, namespace="app-282" and pod="checkout-698c8f5df-bg46s"; there is no 'service' label on these streams, which is why {service="checkout"} matched nothing.
With the corrected selector {acme_service="checkout", namespace="app-282", level="ERROR"}, 4 error-level log lines were returned for the window 2026-11-23T18:09:06Z to 2026-11-23T19:09:06Z.

The metric query sum(count_over_time({acme_service="checkout", namespace="app-282", level="ERROR"}[1h])) evaluated at 2026-11-23T19:09:06Z returned the value 4, independently matching the 4 returned ERROR lines.

The level breakdown for the same one-hour window is ERROR=4, WARN=2, INFO=10, and a per-pod breakdown attributes all 16 of those lines to pod checkout-698c8f5df-bg46s; no other pod or stream appeared in namespace app-282 in that window.

The four ERROR lines are, verbatim from the checkout log: "Payment processor refused: invalid token (txn 9d1f)", "Inventory check timed out for SKU-77481", "Order persistence failed: deadlock on orders table", and "Webhook delivery exhausted retries for partner ACME"; all four were written at 2026-11-23T19:08:33Z by pod checkout-698c8f5df-bg46s.

The four ERROR messages point at distinct dependencies (payment processor, inventory, the orders table/database, and an external webhook partner named ACME), which suggests the single checkout pod's errors could originate outside checkout itself; this is unverified because no log, trace or metric for those dependencies was queried in this Run.

Checkout itself is still logging normal completions alongside the errors in the same window: 10 INFO lines such as "Checkout flow completed for cart 10" were present at 2026-11-23T19:08:33Z, so the 4 ERROR lines are not the entire output of the service in this hour.

gaps: The selector exactly as requested, {service="checkout"}, returned no lines in namespace app-282 for 2026-11-23T18:09:06Z-19:09:06Z; that empty result is a query outcome only and is not evidence of absence of logs.

The count of 4 ERROR lines covers only the one-hour window ending at the authorized window end (2026-11-23T18:09:06Z to 19:09:06Z). The authorized window itself spans 2026-10-24T19:09:06Z to 2026-11-23T19:09:06Z, and no counts were produced for the earlier portion of it, so the error volume over that longer period is unknown.

No logs, traces or metrics were queried for the dependencies named in the ERROR text (payment processor, inventory, orders database, webhook partner ACME), so their state and whether they caused these checkout errors remain unknown.
The change_history integration is not available in this Run, so whether anything changed around 2026-11-23T19:08:33Z could not be checked.
next_steps: If the total error volume matters, run the same count_over_time query over the earlier parts of the authorized window (e.g. day by day) rather than assuming 4 for the whole period.

If the cause matters, query Loki and traces for the services behind the named dependencies (payment, inventory/order persistence, webhook delivery to partner ACME) in the minutes around 2026-11-23T19:08:33Z to see whether they emitted matching errors or elevated latency.

Confirm the intended label convention with whoever owns the Loki pipeline, since dashboards or alerts written against service="checkout" would match nothing while the data lives under acme_service="checkout".
